Lines: The hills at noon smell gently of the thyme, / and each white hive hangs heavy with the light; / I watch the bees; they never mind the time, / and each one lifts a little sun in flight. // The keeper tips the lid and will not speak; / the smoke is set; the hum sinks thick and low. / He takes a tenth of what they made this week, / and leaves the sun in wax; then lets them go. // In winter, when the last thyme sets its seed, / the hive still hums a little, all the same, / and eats the summer that it did not need, / the sun it kept, and lit again: a flame. // Then take a tenth of what the day has made, / and leave the rest as light inside the shade.
